The steps are: Limit speed to 7 knots or less during stern-first landings. Use Rule 15, Rule 17. Use the prowords give-way vessel, stand-on vessel, risk of collision, tugboat, tanker. Hydrodynamic forces increase exponentially with vessel speed.

According to usa/marine_reports/2023/MIR2315.pdf (Incident Report Excerpt): A collision occurred between Tugboat George M and Containership MSC Aquarius during a bow-to-bow maneuver. The steps are: communicate speed limits to the pilot before engaging in maneuvers; then request the assisted vessel to slow down if speeds exceed safe limits. Use Rule 15, Rule 17. Use the prowords give-way vessel, stand-on vessel, risk of collision, tugboat, containership. The maximum safe speed for bow-to-bow maneuvers is 7 knots.

Combined recommendation on TUGBOAT: Hydrodynamic forces increase exponentially with vessel speed. The tugboat's speed increased to 11.6 knots during the maneuver. The maximum safe speed for bow-to-bow maneuvers is 7 knots. Hydrodynamic forces increase exponentially with speed, affecting maneuverability.
